IceBrick8760Design Day by Geography and Supply Temperatures
Advanced thermal management for data centers and AI factories

Size your cooling for the hottest day your site has actually seen

Pick a site and the water temperature your racks are promised. We pull that site's hottest measured day, split the heat between your dry coolers and your chillers hour by hour, and show the mechanical cooling and electrical capacity you have to hold in reserve for it. Then we put an IceBrick thermal store in the loop, charging at night and discharging through the day, and show what that reserve becomes.

Question 1 of 2
Where is your site?

Click the hub closest to your data center. Each one carries 50 years of measured hourly weather (ERA5 (European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts Reanalysis v5), 1976–2025), and the design day is the hottest day in the window you choose further down.

Choose a hub
Question 2 of 2
What is your supply temperature to the racks?

This is the coolant temperature the CDU (coolant distribution unit) delivers to the cold plates. The facility water has to run one CDU approach colder than that, and the loop comes back 10 K warmer. The warmer this number, the more of the day the dry coolers carry on their own.

ASHRAE (American Society of Heating, Refrigerating and Air-Conditioning Engineers) liquid classes W27 to W45 sit inside this range.
Facility water runs this much colder than the rack supply.
All IT heat is taken to liquid. Every duty below scales with it.
